title: Analyzing the Safety of Japanese Large Language Models in Stereotype-Triggering Prompts
findings: Prompts related to religion consistently elicited higher toxicity scores across all three models (Gemma, Qwen, LLM-jp). The English-based model, Gemma, showed a particularly high refusal rate for religious prompts. The Japanese-native model, LLM-jp, generated predominantly positive sentiment for the religion category, in contrast to its negative sentiment for most other social categories.
